question: Does the Commission consider it compatible with the requirements and objectives of Directive 2011/92/EU (as amended) concerning EIA for Member States to regularise long-standing, large-scale industrial activities through retrospective assessment procedures, rather than ensuring assessment prior to development consent?

Does the Commission consider that the use of substitute consent mechanisms risks undermining the preventative and precautionary principles underpinning EU environmental law, particularly where an EIA and appropriate assessment were not carried out before works commenced?
Are Member States required under EU law to ensure that any unlawful environmental damage is fully remedied before considering or granting any form of retrospective or substitute consent?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.10.2026) According to settled case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union, EU law ensuring assessment prior to development consent should remain the rule and only in exceptional circumstances allow the regularisation of operations or measures1.

This case-law of the Court affirms the basic principles underpinning the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Directive2, namely the precautionary principle and the principles that preventive action should be taken, and damages be rectified, at source. Following this established jurisprudence, Member States should nullify the unlawful consequences of a failure to carry out an EIA.

Any such remedial EIA carried out after a project has been completed and has entered into operation, is conditional on there being in place: (i) national rules ensuring that there is no circumvention of EU law, and (ii) a requirement that the remedial EIA takes account not only of the project’s future environmental impact, but also its past impact such as impacts during its construction phase3.
1 Case C-215/06, Commission v Ireland, paragraph 57 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-

content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A62006CA0215). 2 Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1–21, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014, p. 1–18.
